# Message codes: Project metadata

See also: [Message codes](message-codes.md) (the index of every code) and
[Messages and codes](messages.md) (the line grammar, what a code guarantees and
when to trust one).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_message_reference.py; do not edit. -->

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and
`message-codes-values.md` the values.

### `dynamic-field-needs-build`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A [project] field is dynamic and only a build computes it: a PDM
  version source other than a file or SCM tag (a call into the project's code),
  or an sdist's dynamic fields when the archive holds no PKG-INFO to state them.
  Pitloom never runs project code to read metadata.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Read the project without the value: the SBOM records no
  version (or no such field) for it.
- **Tell the user**: which field is not recorded and why, as the line says. A
  built wheel or sdist states the value: an SBOM of it (loom wheel, an sdist
  with PKG-INFO) records it. Do not build or run the project for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: PDM version source <value> is not resolvable without running project code; version not recorded [dynamic-field-needs-build]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: dynamic <metadata-fields> not resolved without PKG-INFO; skipped [dynamic-field-needs-build]
  ```

### `dynamic-field-unusable`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A dynamic [project] field's backend resolver failed: pdm-backend
  reading the version from a file or SCM tag, or flit-core reading the version
  and description from the module without importing it. The failure is the
  resolver's.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Read the project without the value: the SBOM records no
  version (Flit: no version and no description) from the resolver.
- **Tell the user**: which resolver failed and its failure, as the line says.
  The file the backend reads is often missing or malformed (a version file, a
  module docstring); they fix it and generate again. Do not edit the project for
  them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: PDM dynamic version not resolved; <failure> [dynamic-field-unusable]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: Flit dynamic metadata not resolved; <failure> [dynamic-field-unusable]
  ```

### `installed-metadata-ambiguous`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: More than one .dist-info or .egg-info directory in the project
  directory names the project (an old install left beside a new one).
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Used the one the line names: a .dist-info before an
  .egg-info, then by name, so the same directories give the same choice.
- **Tell the user**: which directories were found and which was used, as the
  line says. They remove the stale ones and generate again. Do not delete
  anything for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: several installed-metadata candidates (<files>); used <entry> [installed-metadata-ambiguous]
  ```

### `installed-metadata-unusable`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A .dist-info or .egg-info directory in the project directory, read
  to complete the declared metadata, is not this project's: it has no METADATA
  (or PKG-INFO), or names no project or another one (a renamed project, a stale
  install). One whose file cannot be read says file-unreadable, for the project
  metadata.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Ignored that directory: the SBOM takes nothing from it.
- **Tell the user**: which directory was ignored and why, as the line says. A
  stale one is removed, or the project reinstalled (pip install -e .), and the
  SBOM generated again. Do not delete or install anything for them; ask first,
  and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: <entry> has no <file>; ignored [installed-metadata-unusable]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: <entry> declares name <name>, not the project's; ignored [installed-metadata-unusable]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: <entry> declares no name; ignored [installed-metadata-unusable]
  ```

### `metadata-conflict`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: Two sources of the project's metadata give one field two real
  values: setup.py and setup.cfg (a setup() keyword overrides the setup.cfg
  option, as setuptools does), or the declared metadata and an installed
  .dist-info or .egg-info (a stale install). The DIR= line with 'names project'
  is an embed with a project directory (embed-wheel --project-dir) whose project
  is not the wheel's, by PEP 503 name; it prints since 0.25.0.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Recorded the value the line keeps and both values as a
  conflict in the field's provenance. For an embed's project directory, took the
  authors from the wheel's METADATA, not from the project.
- **Tell the user**: which field disagrees, what was kept and what dropped, as
  the line says. They make the sources agree (or reinstall the project) and
  generate again. Do not edit the project for them; ask first, and with nobody
  to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: <field>: setup.py and setup.cfg disagree; kept setup.py's <kept>, dropped setup.cfg's <dropped> [metadata-conflict]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: <field>: setup.py and setup.cfg disagree; kept setup.cfg's <kept>, dropped setup.py's <dropped> [metadata-conflict]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: <field>: declared and installed metadata disagree; kept the declared <kept>, dropped the installed <dropped> [metadata-conflict]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: names project <project-value>, not the wheel's <wheel-value>; authors from the wheel METADATA [metadata-conflict]
  ```

### `metadata-invalid`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A project metadata value is not what its format allows: a [project]
  that pyproject-metadata refuses (its words), a [project] or [tool.poetry] that
  is no table, a name that is no string, a version with a number too long to
  parse, a [project] with no name, a value of the wrong type, a setup() keyword
  Pitloom cannot read statically, a tool.setuptools.dynamic entry that is no
  {file = ...} table, or a requirements file a setting lists that is not there.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: As an ERROR, wrote nothing: the command exits 1 (the Action
  step fails), the library raises ValueError carrying the code. As a WARNING,
  read on without the value: a wrong type is ignored; a setup() keyword is
  treated as undeclared, so a lower-priority source may give the field; a
  [project] with no name leaves setup.cfg and setup.py to name the project; a
  listed file not there gives no requirements; a [tool.poetry] relayed from a
  Poetry read skips Poetry's gap-fill, while poetry.lock's pins still apply.
  'loom fragment list' says a refused [project] or too long a number as a
  WARNING too, and lists the fragments with SAME_DOCUMENT=-.
- **Tell the user**: which value is refused or ignored and what was expected, as
  the line says; a WARNING leaves the field out of the SBOM or takes it from
  another source. They fix the value in the file named and generate again. Do
  not edit the project for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it
  only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: <field> is <got>, expected <expected> [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <field> is <got>, expected <expected> [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <field> is <got>, expected <expected>; ignored [metadata-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: not valid [project] metadata; <failure> [metadata-invalid]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: <field> has a number over <number> digits [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: not valid [project] metadata; <failure> [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <field> has a number over <number> digits [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: [project] has no name; read setup.cfg and setup.py instead [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: setup() keyword <name> is not read; treated as undeclared [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: setup() keyword <name> is not a literal; treated as undeclared [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: setup() keyword <name> has a value Pitloom does not read (<value>); treated as undeclared [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: setup() keyword <name> is blank; treated as undeclared [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <field> is not a table with 'file'; ignored [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <field> has 'attr', not supported for requirements; ignored [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: listed by <field>, not found; skipped [metadata-invalid]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: listed by <field>, not a file name; skipped [metadata-invalid]
  ```

### `metadata-malformed`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A setup.py is not Python the parser of the Python Pitloom runs on
  can read: a syntax error, a NUL byte, or an expression nested too deeply for
  it. The failure is the parser's. The nested line is the line of a module that
  a setup.cfg attr: directive names, too deeply nested to parse alone.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: As an ERROR, wrote nothing: the command exits 1 (the Action
  step fails), the library raises ValueError carrying the code. As a WARNING,
  read the project without it: a setup.py that does not parse while setup.cfg
  names the project leaves setup.cfg read alone; one read for pyproject.toml's
  dynamic fields fills none of them; a nested attr: line leaves the field it was
  read for unset, said once per file and field per process.
- **Tell the user**: which file does not parse and the parser's failure, as the
  line says. They fix the syntax (setup.py runs as Python 3) or write the value
  as a literal, and generate again. Do not edit the project for them; ask first,
  and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: not valid Python; <failure> [metadata-malformed]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: not valid Python; <failure> [metadata-malformed]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <name> line too deeply nested to parse; skipped for <field> [metadata-malformed]
  ```

### `metadata-no-effect`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A project declares something its build backend does not read: a
  [tool.poetry] table or keys Poetry ignores because [project] declares the
  same, [tool.poetry] keys under another build backend, or pip option lines (-r,
  --index-url) in a requirements file setuptools reads for
  tool.setuptools.dynamic.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Read the project as its build backend does, without them.
- **Tell the user**: which declaration has no effect and why, as the line says;
  the SBOM states what a build would. They move or remove it if it was meant to
  apply. Do not edit the project for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <field> not read: Poetry reads [project] <metadata-fields> instead; ignored [metadata-no-effect]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: [tool.poetry] <entries> not read: build-backend <backend> does not read them; ignored [metadata-no-effect]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: <field>: pip option lines <entries>, which setuptools does not accept; skipped [metadata-no-effect]
  ```

### `project-name-missing`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: No project name is found where the project's build backend reads
  it: a Poetry project names it in neither [tool.poetry] nor [project]; a
  setuptools project in neither setup.cfg [metadata] nor a setup(name=...)
  string literal (a name computed by code is not read). A setup.py that does not
  parse says metadata-malformed first.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: As an ERROR, wrote nothing: the command exits 1 (the Action
  step fails), the library raises ValueError carrying the code. The setuptools
  line raises FileNotFoundError, also carrying the code. As a WARNING, a Poetry
  read for poetry.lock's pins skipped Poetry's gap-fill and still applied the
  pins; 'loom fragment list' says any of them and lists the fragments with
  SAME_DOCUMENT=-.
- **Tell the user**: that the project has no name Pitloom can read, and where it
  looked, as the line says. They declare name in [project] (or [tool.poetry],
  setup.cfg [metadata], or setup() as a string literal) and generate again. Do
  not edit the project for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it
  only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: neither [tool.poetry] nor [project] has a project name [project-name-missing]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: neither [tool.poetry] nor [project] has a project name [project-name-missing]
  ERROR: DIR=<dir>: no project name in setup.cfg [metadata] or a literal setup(name=...) [project-name-missing]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: [metadata] has no project name [project-name-missing]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: no project name: setup(name=...) is not a string literal [project-name-missing]
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: no project name in setup.cfg [metadata] or a literal setup(name=...) [project-name-missing]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: [metadata] has no project name [project-name-missing]
  WARNING: FILE=<file>: no project name: setup(name=...) is not a string literal [project-name-missing]
  ```
